name: eBay used NVIDIA Tesla P40 24GB (multi-option-listing trap priced in)
price_basis: USED, bare passive PCIe card, no fan shroud. $290 = the realistic clean-single-listing band: dedicated P40 single-listings cluster $273-325 and the P40 selection INSIDE multi-option 'P4/P40/K80/M40' listings runs ~$273-310. The ~$105-140 headline prices are MULTI-OPTION LISTINGS where $104.98 buys the P4 8GB variant, NOT the P40. ASKING price, not sold. PERISHABLE-FIGURE STAMP: OBSERVED 2026-10-14. RE-VERIFY BY: 2027-01-14.
lead_time_basis: lead_time_weeks is null because this is a secondary market priced per listing.
export_control_regime: EAR 3A001 or EAR99 (legacy Pascal below 3A090.a thresholds)
export_control_note: Legacy Pascal part below the advanced-computing thresholds; general EAR applies.
notes: Budget ~$110-150 ONLY if you accept the multi-listing lottery (headline price buys the wrong SKU); ~$280+ for a clean dedicated unit. Newegg refurb floor $397.99 (separate record used-nvidia-tesla-p40-market). The cheapest way to hold a 24-32B GGUF, with slow prefill - Pascal has no FP16 tensor cores so GGUF INT8/Q4 DP4A is the only path. Gotchas: passive card needs shroud+blower, EPS-12V 8-pin NOT PCIe 8-pin, needs Above-4G/ReBAR BIOS.
